Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.relations

Class RelationMap<M extends Model>

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.relations.RelationMap<M>
Type Parameters:
M - the model class the relations start from
public final class RelationMap<M extends Model> extends Object
The relations a model class can load by name, in the order they were added; what a model returns from relations(). 

 protected RelationMap<Post> relations() {
     return RelationMap.of(Post.class).add("comments", Post::comments).add("author", Post::author);
 }

Laravel finds a relation by calling the method of that name. Java has no such call without reflection, so the names that with, load, has and lazy loading use are listed here instead. A map is checked once per model class, the first time a relation of the class is resolved by name; a bad entry then fails with InvalidRelationException.

Immutable: add(String, RelationFactory) returns a new map and leaves this one as it is. Safe to share between threads, provided the factories are.

    • add

      public RelationMap<M> add(String name, RelationFactory<? super M> factory)
      Returns a new map with one more relation, after the ones already added.

      The name is checked with the rest of the map the first time the model class resolves a relation: it must not be empty and must not hold . or :, which eager load paths use.

      Parameters:
      name - the relation name, as with and has take it, never null
      factory - builds the relation for a model, such as Post::comments, never null
      Returns:
      a new map, never null; this map is unchanged
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if the map already has a relation of that name

    • resolve

      public Relation<?,?> resolve(String name, Model model)
      Builds a relation by name for a model and gives it that name.

      This runs the factory and nothing else. A model's own relation(name) also checks the map once per class, and is what applications call.

      Parameters:
      name - the relation name, never null
      model - the parent model, never null, an instance of modelClass()
      Returns:
      a new, unconstrained relation, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if the model is not an instance of the map's model class
      RelationNotFoundException - if the map has no relation of that name
      InvalidRelationException - if the factory returns null
